blocks.heading: How to seek finance
blocks.text: Begin by identifying the amount needed, its purpose, when it is required and when the business can repay or provide a return. Prepare a business plan and realistic cash-flow forecast, supported by accounts or sales evidence where available. Approach a suitable provider: a lender for a loan, shareholders for equity, a supplier for trade credit, an asset provider for leasing or an institution offering eligible support. Present the proposal and information that the provider needs rather than simply requesting money. A lender may request security, repayment evidence and information about existing borrowing. An equity investor needs to understand ownership rights, risks and expected returns. Compare the total cost, duration, conditions and consequences for control before accepting an offer. Obtain agreed terms and monitor the commitments after funds are supplied. The process does not guarantee acceptance; an attractive idea can still have weak repayment prospects or fail a provider’s eligibility criteria.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Sola Repairs seeks finance for a diagnostic machine. It has records of paid repair work but has not estimated the timing of future receipts. The owner should prepare the machine cost, expected additional receipts and a cash forecast before approaching a bank. The bank can then assess whether scheduled repayments fit likely cash inflows. Sola should compare the offered loan with leasing rather than choosing whichever quote mentions the smallest monthly payment without checking duration and total cost.
